chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

'Which thing is God Greater than?' I said, 'God is Greater than everything.' He said, 'Was there then something, so that He would be greater than it?' I said, 'And what is it (the correct meaning)?' He said, 'God is Greater than to be described.'

key_terms.اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ: Allahu Akbar — traditionally translated 'God is Greatest'; the Imam redefines it as 'God is too great to be described'
key_terms.ثَمَّ شَيْءٌ: was there something — the Imam's rhetorical point that comparing God to things implies the prior existence of those things alongside God
key_terms.يُوصَفَ: to be described/attributed — God transcends all human description and comparison

ai.seo_question: What does 'Allahu Akbar' really mean according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this theological dialogue, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) corrects a common misunderstanding of the takbir formula 'Allahu Akbar.' When his companion Jumai' ibn Umayr interpreted it to mean 'God is greater than everything' — implying a comparison between God and created things — the Imam redirected him. The Imam's correction establishes that God transcends all comparisons; the formula means 'God is too great to be described (by human language).' This teaching reflects the Shia theological principle of tanzih (divine transcendence), affirming that no attribute or comparison can fully capture God's reality.
